rawRetro.summary: Repair 4. Fixed the 10 ESLint errors that failed the factory lint stage in server/providers/service-domain.ts and server/providers/service-support.ts, then removed the build blockers the same in-progress feature had left behind: the service-ticket-acceptance Workflow DSL imported three run/condition modules that did not exist and called finalize() on the node-less builder, so the server typecheck and the workflow checker failed. Implemented the missing handlers (is-urgent, register-normal-acceptance, register-urgent-acceptance plus a shared acceptance helper that moves the ticket to pending_process, records the branch note and notifies the assignee idempotently) and finalized the tree that actually holds the node. Also restored the .ts specifiers the source-loaded seed and seed-data require, which had reverted to .js and made tests/logic/app-server.test.ts fail at seed load. Verified: full ESLint clean, pnpm typecheck clean, pnpm nocobase workflow check (3 nodes), all 245 tests, pnpm build (1 workflow artifact) and pnpm nocobase db apply all pass. The business feature layer itself (server routes, client pages, ServiceDomain registration, Scheduler/AI wiring) is still absent and remains the open acceptance gap.

improvements.title: `as never` casts hid an inference mismatch instead of a type error
improvements.detail: server/authorization/resources.ts used `as never` in six record-access resolvers and on the composite registration call. The lint rule proved the resolver assertions unnecessary and removing one of them exposed that `define(resource)` could not accept the union of builder types. The runtime intent was already `build()`-based, so the casts were masking an avoidable generic-inference problem.
improvements.suggestedChange: Prefer passing the concrete built value (`resource.build()`) or annotating the collection with the framework's accepted parameter type instead of `as never`.

improvements.title: No guard against .js relative imports from source-loaded seeds and migrations
improvements.detail: server/** may import .js because it runs from compiled dist, but database/** seeds and migrations are dynamically imported from TypeScript source by the app-server task loader, where Node's native type stripping resolves only .ts specifiers. A .js specifier pointing at a .ts file compiles and only fails at application startup with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND.
improvements.suggestedChange: Add a lint or check for relative imports under database/** that requires the .ts extension (or teach the seed/migration loader to resolve .js to .ts) so the mistake fails at author time rather than at runtime.

improvements.title: A startup registration function existed but had no call site
improvements.detail: server/authorization/resources.ts exported registerServiceAuthorization(), but nothing invoked it. The omission was invisible until seeded grants were validated in AuthorizationProvider.start(), which then failed on every composite action. The declarations were correct; only the lifecycle hook was missing.
improvements.suggestedChange: When a module exports a register*/define* function meant to run at startup, wire it to a named ServiceProvider in the same change, or export the provider instead of a bare function.

improvements.title: A key used by a component but absent from en-US is caught only by a test
improvements.detail: en-US is the source-of-truth locale shape, so zh-CN is typed against AppResource and a missing key there is a compile error. A key present in neither locale, however, compiles and is only caught by tests/logic/app-locale-coverage.test.ts.
improvements.suggestedChange: Optionally type component translation keys against AppResource or add a check that every t() key exists in en-US, so a missing key fails at build time.

improvements.title: Source-loaded database tasks must use .ts specifiers, and the fix regressed
improvements.detail: Repair 2 had fixed database/main/seeds/..._create_service_permission_sets.ts and database/seed-data/permission-sets.ts to import .ts, because seeds and migrations are dynamically imported from TypeScript source (Node type stripping) where a .js specifier pointing at a .ts file throws ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND. Repair 3 rewrote both back to .js, so the seed-load failure returned in tests/logic/app-server.test.ts. The tsconfigs already allow importing .ts and rewrite it on emit, so the guard below would have caught it.
improvements.suggestedChange: Add a lint/check that relative imports under database/** must use the .ts extension (and the opposite, .js, under server/**), so this recurring mistake fails at author time.

issues.title: eslint @typescript-eslint/no-unnecessary-type-assertion in server/authorization/resources.ts
issues.symptom: pnpm lint failed with 8 errors, all 'This assertion is unnecessary since the receiver accepts the original type of the expression' at lines 521, 540, 547, 560, 579, 596, 609 and 638.
issues.rootCause: Eight `as never` assertions were unnecessary for the compiler. Once the assertion on `authz.compositeResources.define(resource as never)` was removed, TypeScript reported TS2345: the `serviceResources` `as const` array is a union of concretely-typed `CompositeResourceBuilder<...>` values that cannot bind the generic `define<A extends CompositeResourceActions>(definition)`. The `as never` had been silencing this genuine inference limitation.
issues.resolution: Removed the seven unnecessary `as never` casts (six resolver filters plus the `define` argument) and registered composites with `authz.compositeResources.define(resource.build())`, matching what the framework's own `define` does internally for a builder. Verified with `pnpm exec eslint server/authorization/resources.ts --max-warnings 0`, `pnpm exec tsc -p tsconfig.server.json --noEmit` and `pnpm exec prettier --check server/authorization/resources.ts`, all clean.

issues.title: confirmDialog translation keys missing from both locales
issues.symptom: tests/logic/app-locale-coverage.test.ts failed two tests ('translates every key the application uses into English' and '... into Chinese') reporting confirmDialog.cancel and confirmDialog.failed, both from components/confirm-dialog.tsx, as untranslated.
issues.rootCause: client/components/confirm-dialog.tsx reads t('confirmDialog.cancel') and t('confirmDialog.failed'), but neither client/locales/en-US.ts nor client/locales/zh-CN.ts declared a confirmDialog group.
issues.resolution: Added confirmDialog: { cancel, failed } to both client/locales/en-US.ts and client/locales/zh-CN.ts. tests/logic/app-locale-coverage.test.ts and the full suite pass.

issues.title: Seed relative import used a .js specifier the source runtime cannot resolve
issues.symptom: tests/logic/app-server.test.ts failed the tests 'starts a fresh Default without example tables or APIs' and 'serves Users and API Keys with the application authentication and permissions' with AppDatabaseTaskError: Database seeds failed for connection "main": Cannot find module '.../database/seed-data/permission-sets.js' imported from '.../database/main/seeds/202610010001_create_service_permission_sets.ts' (ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND).
issues.rootCause: Seeds and migrations are dynamically imported from TypeScript source by the @nocobase/app-server task loader, so Node's native type stripping resolves .ts specifiers but not a .js specifier pointing at a .ts file. server/** uses .js specifiers because it loads from compiled dist, but that convention does not hold for source-loaded database tasks.
issues.resolution: Changed the seed to import '../../seed-data/permission-sets.ts' and seed-data/permission-sets.ts to import '../../server/authorization/resources.ts'. tsconfig.server.json enables allowImportingTsExtensions and rewriteRelativeImportExtensions, so a build still emits .js; verified with a temporary tsc emit.

issues.title: registerServiceAuthorization had no caller, so seeded composite grants failed validation
issues.symptom: Once the seed loaded, tests/logic/app-server.test.ts failed with 'Authorization has invalid stored grants: Unknown composite resource action: service.ticket.view', listing every service composite action (service.assistant.ask, service.ledger.manage, service.knowledge.view, and so on).
issues.rootCause: server/authorization/resources.ts defines the service composites, record access and collections, but its registerServiceAuthorization() export was never invoked. The seeded permission sets grant those composite actions, and AuthorizationProvider.start() rejects a grant whose composite resource action is undefined, so the application could not start.
issues.resolution: Added server/providers/service-authorization.ts, an application ServiceProvider whose boot() resolves authorizationToken and calls registerServiceAuthorization(), and registered it in server/providers/index.ts. Application providers boot before startAll validates grants. The provider is a no-op when the authorization plugin is not registered, which the runtime-contribution test relies on.

issues.title: 10 ESLint errors in the new service domain providers
issues.symptom: pnpm lint failed with 10 errors: 4 @typescript-eslint/no-unnecessary-type-assertion (`as never` on repository update object literals) and 4 no-unsafe-member-access/no-unsafe-assignment in the dashboard grouping at server/providers/service-domain.ts lines 496/540/705/758/1939-1942, one no-useless-assignment at 1215 (`let failure: string | null = null`), and one unnecessary assertion in server/providers/service-support.ts line 50.
issues.rootCause: The repository updateOne/values typings already accept the object literal without `as never`, the dashboard ternary `isSupervisor ? await this.groupIndex() : new Map()` widened to Map<any,any>, and `failure` is assigned on every reachable path so the initializer was dead. The `decision.conditions?.database as unknown as ScopedPolicies` cast did not change the type either.
issues.resolution: Removed the five unnecessary assertions, typed the fallback map as `new Map<number, EngineerGroupRow>()`, and changed the initializer to `let failure: string | null;`. Full `pnpm exec eslint . --max-warnings 0 --ignore-pattern '.github/**'` is clean.

issues.title: service-ticket-acceptance Workflow referenced missing modules and finalized an empty tree
issues.symptom: `tsc -p tsconfig.server.json` exited 2 with TS2307 for ./server/is-urgent, ./server/register-normal-acceptance and ./server/register-urgent-acceptance; the next pipeline stage after lint would have failed on it.
issues.rootCause: The workflow definition was written but its three handler modules were never created. It also declared `const flow = workflow(...)`, derived `classified = flow.addNode(...)` and then called `flow.finalize()`, discarding the only builder that held the node, so even once the modules existed the definition would have compiled to zero nodes.
issues.resolution: Added the three handler modules and a shared acceptance helper that writes pending_process, acceptanceStatus='succeeded', the branch note/mode and notifies the assignee under an idempotency key; added the member-by-member FlowContext interface; finalized `classified` instead of `flow`. `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm nocobase workflow check workflows/service-ticket-acceptance` (3 nodes) and `pnpm build` (1 artifact with all run modules) pass.

issues.title: Source-loaded seed import regressed to a .js specifier
issues.symptom: tests/logic/app-server.test.ts failed the 'starts a fresh Default' and 'serves Users and API Keys' tests with AppDatabaseTaskError: Cannot find module '.../database/seed-data/permission-sets.js' imported from the seed .ts file.
issues.rootCause: The seed and database/seed-data/permission-sets.ts import each other with a .js specifier, but the @nocobase/app-server task loader imports them from TypeScript source, where Node type stripping resolves .ts and not a .js pointing at a .ts. Repair 2 had used .ts; repair 3 rewrote it back to .js.
issues.resolution: Restored `../../seed-data/permission-sets.ts` and `../../server/authorization/resources.ts`. The base server tsconfig rewrites .ts to .js on emit (verified in dist), and tests/logic/app-server.test.ts (28) plus the full suite (41 files, 245 tests) pass.

issues.title: Business feature layer is not wired: no application routes or pages for the after-sales system
issues.symptom: server/routes/index.ts still exports an empty array and client/routes.ts declares only home and the auth pages, so the verify-3 browser pass found no customers/devices/tickets/inspections/knowledge/dashboard pages and 404s for the service APIs. ServiceDomain exists but serviceDomainToken is not registered by any provider, so the domain service is unreachable.
issues.rootCause: The domain/data/workflow layer was implemented ahead of the HTTP and UI layers; the application surface that exposes them was never added.
